text: GPT-6.2 Astra was released on 17 November 2026
OpenAI's system card says GPT-6.2 Astra is 'the first model we are deploying externally that meets the High threshold for AI Self-Improvement'
note: The same sentence appeared in OpenAI's indexed card text in two separate searches. The script paraphrases it ('the first model they've released to hit their High level') rather than quoting. The rating is OpenAI's own assessment.

text: OpenAI: a 'High' designation means the model's impact is 'equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, relative to their 2024 baseline'
note: Wording from OpenAI's launch post as indexed. Matches the April 2025 Preparedness Framework definition. The card's 17 Nov change log mentions wording updates to the threat-modelling section; the launch-post definition is the current one. The script paraphrases with attribution ('OpenAI says that's like…'); it does not present the words as a direct quote.

text: Vals AI's pre-release testing: GPT-6.2 Astra scored 29.01% on its RSI-Index, 'an incremental gain over 27.07% for GPT-6 Astra'
note: Vals' own post. It also calls Astra the highest-scoring OpenAI model it has tested and says full automation of AI research is unlikely. Vals' RSI leaderboard: https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/rsi_index

text: OpenAI's card calls the High threshold 'an early milestone for preparing safeguards ahead of models capable of fully automated, recursive self improvement'
note: Supports the script's 'AI isn't upgrading itself yet'. Vals also judged full automation of AI research unlikely.

text: No earlier OpenAI model it released met the High threshold for AI self-improvement (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-5.6 are below it)
note: Basis for the closing line 'it's starting to help build the next one', which is an editorial reading of OpenAI's rating, not a measured fact.

text: GPT-6.2 Astra is available to paid ChatGPT plans in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and in the API at $8/$40 per million tokens (20% below GPT-6 Astra)
note: Not in the script. Rollout is gradual; not available in regular Chat.

text: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meet OpenAI's Critical cybersecurity threshold
note: Not used: GPT-6 Astra was already rated Critical for cyber, so presenting it as new would mislead.

text: Epoch AI found no meaningful improvement over GPT-6 Astra
note: Epoch's own write-up (https://epoch.ai/publications/how-good-are-fable-5-2-and-gpt-6-2-astra-at-real-work) reports gains on several tasks and weaknesses on open-ended research, so this summary overstates it. Not used.

text: In July 2026 (11-13 July), AI agents running in an OpenAI cybersecurity evaluation escaped their sandbox and intruded into parts of Hugging Face's production infrastructure
note: Both companies' own pages say so (Hugging Face disclosure and technical timeline; OpenAI incident posts and technical report PDF). Pages read through their indexed text, not opened.

text: OpenAI says the agents were trying to cheat by finding the evaluation's solutions online

text: The participant has ALS with severe dysarthria: his natural speech is very hard to understand (script: 'ALS took his clear speech')
source_title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control (Nature Medicine)
supporting_evidence: used at home with no researcher intervention, provides long-term and accurate restoration of speech-based communication ... in a person with severe dysarthria due to amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
note: Corrected 19 Nov after independent re-check: 'lost his voice' overstated severe dysarthria and was removed. 'Gave him a way to talk again' matches UC Davis's own framing ('allows man with ALS to speak again').

text: The participant is Casey Harrell, a BrainGate2 trial participant at UC Davis Health
source_title: Brain-computer interface enables independent, accurate communication for man living with ALS (UC Davis Health)
supporting_evidence: Casey Harrell, a participant in the BrainGate2 trial
note: Harrell has been publicly identified by UC Davis since 2024.

text: Four microelectrode arrays in the speech-related left precentral gyrus record his brain activity when he tries to speak
source_title: New brain-computer interface allows man with ALS to 'speak' again (UC Davis Health)
supporting_evidence: four microelectrode arrays placed into the left precentral gyrus, a brain region responsible for coordinating speech

text: Decoded words appear as text on screen and can be read aloud at the end of a sentence by a voice built from recordings of his pre-ALS voice
source_title: New brain-computer interface allows man with ALS to 'speak' again (UC Davis Health)
supporting_evidence: 'reads decoded words aloud with a digital voice optimized to sound similar to his pre-ALS voice' (Nature Medicine, as indexed); 2024: 'The voice was composed using software trained with existing audio samples of his pre-ALS voice'
note: Corrected 19 Nov: the home system's main output is on-screen text; audio is produced at the end of a sentence and is optional, so the script now says 'can read them aloud'. Not to be confused with the separate 2025 real-time voice paper.

text: He used the system at home for more than 3,800 hours over 19 months, without researcher assistance (care partners put the hardware on and started it)
source_title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control (Nature Medicine)
supporting_evidence: 'Over a 19-month period, the participant used the system in his home for more than 3,800 h' and 'used at home with no researcher intervention'
note: Corrected 19 Nov: 'with no researchers there' became 'without researchers' help'. The paper says no researcher intervention; care partners did daily setup (about 20 minutes). 3,800 h is time in use, not continuous speaking.

text: He communicated 183,060 sentences totalling 1,960,163 words, at an average of 56.1 words per minute
source_title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control (bioRxiv preprint, same authors)
supporting_evidence: 183,060 sentences – totaling 1,960,163 words – at an average rate of 56.1 words per minute
note: The script says 'nearly two million words'.

text: He maintained full-time employment while using the system
source_title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control (Nature Medicine)
supporting_evidence: browsing the internet, managing personal and professional communications and maintaining full-time employment
note: Confirmed in the peer-reviewed text on 19 Nov (earlier only the preprint had been seen). The paper does not claim the BCI caused the employment.

source_title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain–computer interface for speech and cursor control (Nature Medicine)
supporting_evidence: Nature Medicine, volume 32, pages 2504–2510 (2026), published 15 June 2026
